title: Crashlytics
objectives: Understand Crashlytics via a real-life analogy
Capture fatal + non-fatal errors from Dart + native layers
Attach breadcrumbs, custom keys, user identifiers
Symbolicate stack traces reliably in CI
Interpret crash-free-users / velocity alerts and act on them

sections.markdown:
**Think of Crashlytics as the CCTV + black-box recorder for your app.**

A plane crashes. Investigators don't guess — they open the **flight data recorder** (all the parameters the plane was under) + the **cockpit voice recorder** (what the crew was doing) and rebuild the last few minutes. That's Crashlytics.

- **Fatal crash** — the plane broke apart. Someone must fix it before next flight.
- **Non-fatal error** — engine warning light; the plane landed safely, but the ground crew still logs it and looks for a pattern.
- **Custom keys** (`screen`, `feature_flag`, `tenant`) — the flight parameters. Without them you know the plane crashed but not what it was doing.
- **Breadcrumbs (logs)** — the cockpit voice recorder. The last N events before impact.
- **User identifier** — the flight number. Lets you tie a report to a specific customer complaint.
- **Symbolication** — turning obfuscated stack frames like `_ZN5app3barEv` back into `home_screen.dart:42:AddToCart.onPressed`. Without symbols, the black box is just noise.
- **Crash-free users %** — the airline's safety KPI. 99.5% crash-free means 5 users in 1000 saw a crash; below 99% and passengers start choosing other airlines.
- **Velocity alerts** — the tower calling you the moment 3 flights of the same model report the same warning within an hour. Not tomorrow's report — right now.

**Why every mobile team wires this on day one:** without Crashlytics, prod crashes are invisible until a user emails you. With it, you learn about a regression 60 seconds after it starts, know exactly which release + device + code path, and can auto-rollback via Remote Config before it spreads.

**Firebase Crashlytics** is a managed crash-reporting SDK. On every crash it captures the **stack trace + device state + custom keys + breadcrumbs + user identifier + app/release version**, uploads to Firebase, deduplicates by **stack signature** (crashes with the same fingerprint = one issue), and computes **crash-free-users %** and **crash-free-sessions %** — the industry-standard mobile stability KPIs. Also captures **non-fatal errors** (handled exceptions you still want to see) and **ANRs** on Android. Free tier is generous; per-project quota only.

sections.markdown: ## Complete Flutter setup

## Symbolication — the #1 thing devs get wrong

A crash with symbols:

```
NoSuchMethodError: The method 'firstWhere' was called on null.
#0 CartScreen.build (package:app/screens/cart.dart:87:23)
#1 StatelessElement.build (framework.dart:5041:28)
```

A crash without symbols:

```
EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) at 0x0000000102b3f4c8
#0 __ZN5dart:app__vt_23_x (_kDartSymbolStripped)
#1 __ZN5dart:app__vt_9_a (_kDartSymbolStripped)
```

Second one is useless. To get the first you must upload:

- **Android** — the **ProGuard/R8 mapping file** + the **native symbols zip** for NDK code. Gradle plugin auto-uploads on `assembleRelease` if `firebaseCrashlytics { mappingFileUploadEnabled true }` is set. Also enable `nativeSymbolUploadEnabled true`.
- **iOS** — the **dSYM bundle**. Xcode uploads it via the Crashlytics **Run Script build phase**. On modern Xcode + Bitcode-off setups, use the `upload-symbols` script.
- **Flutter** — Flutter obfuscates on `--obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols`. Upload the `symbols/` directory via `firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload`.

**Automate all three in CI on every release build** — never manually. A single missed upload = a whole release worth of unreadable crashes.
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Missing symbol uploads.** Every release build must upload dSYM + mapping + Flutter debug-info. Automate in CI; add a step that FAILS the build if upload fails.

**Mistake 2: No custom keys.** Reports show `NullPointerException` in `Iterable.first` — 400 different bugs look identical. Add `screen`, `feature_flag`, `tenant`, `network_state`, and you triage in seconds.

**Mistake 3: PII in logs / custom keys.** Never log emails, phone numbers, auth tokens, or full user payloads. Store the UID only (pseudonymous), and DELETE the identifier on sign-out (`setUserIdentifier('')`).
**Mistake 4: Reporting in debug builds.** Pollutes issue counts and slows startup. Gate with `!kDebugMode` and enable via `setCrashlyticsCollectionEnabled`.
**Mistake 5: Ignoring non-fatals.** Every handled exception you silently swallow is a bug you'll never learn about. Record it as non-fatal + fix later.
**Mistake 6: No opt-out.** Under GDPR / DPDPA, some users must be able to disable telemetry. Wire a toggle to `setCrashlyticsCollectionEnabled`.
**Mistake 7: Trusting one crash-free-users number.** Slice it by app version, device, country, tenant. A prod-wide 99.6% can hide a 12% number on Redmi devices in India.
**Mistake 8: No velocity alerts.** By the time you check the dashboard, thousands of users crashed. Wire Slack / PagerDuty alerts on session-count velocity.
## Best practices
**1. Wire in main().** All three of `FlutterError.onError`, `PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError`, and `runZonedGuarded` — one alone leaks errors.
**2. Always set custom keys.** `screen`, `tenant`, `remote_config_variant`, `network_state`, `is_offline`.
**3. Automate symbol uploads in CI.** Fastlane / GitHub Actions / Codemagic — every release build, no exceptions.
**4. Record non-fatals for handled errors.** Don't swallow silently.
**5. Set a crash-free-users SLO.** e.g., >99.5% before shipping. Block release if regressing.
**6. Wire velocity alerts.** Slack / PagerDuty on new signatures or session-count spikes.
**7. Correlate with Analytics + Performance.** Same UID + custom keys tie crash → session events → slow trace.
**8. Provide opt-out.** Respect GDPR / DPDPA telemetry consent.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy) — Wire Crashlytics.** Add SDK; call `crash()` in debug; verify report + symbolicated stack appears within 5 minutes.
**Practice 2 (Easy) — Non-fatal.** Throw a handled exception; log via `recordError(fatal: false)`; find it under Non-fatals filter.
**Practice 3 (Medium) — Custom keys + breadcrumbs.** Set `screen`, `tenant`, add `log()` breadcrumbs; force a crash; verify all appear on the report.
**Practice 4 (Medium) — CI symbol upload.** Add a GitHub Actions job that runs `firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload` on every tag. Break it intentionally + verify it fails.
**Practice 5 (Hard) — Velocity alert integration.** Wire a Slack webhook from a Cloud Function that watches new signatures via BigQuery + posts on regression.
**Practice 6 (Expert) — Auto-rollback.** Combine Crashlytics velocity alert → Cloud Function → Remote Config flip → app rolls back to previous variant. Test end-to-end.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What are crash-free users and crash-free sessions? Which do you SLO on?**

**A:** **Crash-free users %** = percent of unique users in the window who saw ZERO crashes. **Crash-free sessions %** = same for sessions. Sessions is always ≥ users (one user with 10 sessions and 1 crash is 0% crash-free by user but 90% by session). **SLO on crash-free users** — that's what impacts store rating and revenue. Typical bar: **99.5% before shipping, alert on drop below 99% or a > 0.2 pp regression release-over-release.** Slice by app version + device tier + country before making conclusions — the aggregate can hide a 20% crash rate on cheap Android devices.

**Q2: Fatal vs non-fatal — what's the difference and how do you use each?**

**A:** **Fatal** = the app process died — automatic capture; user sees a launcher crash. Counts against **crash-free-users %**. **Non-fatal** = you caught the exception, returned an error to the user, but want visibility — send via `recordError(fatal: false)`. Does NOT count against crash-free-users; shows under a separate 'Non-fatals' tab. **Use non-fatals for:** API 5xx, JSON parse failures, image load errors, unexpected states. **Use fatals for:** anything you can't recover from. **Bonus:** Flutter's SDK also has `recordError(fatal: true)` which converts a Dart exception into a *recorded fatal* — reported like a native crash but the Dart isolate can recover. That's what `FlutterError.onError = recordFlutterFatalError` uses.

**Q3: Why must you upload dSYM / ProGuard mapping / Flutter debug-info, and how do you automate it?**

**A:** Release builds are **obfuscated + minified**. Without the corresponding **symbol files**, stack traces look like `_ZN5app3barEv` — meaningless. Symbolication maps them back to `CartScreen.build:87:23`. **Files by platform:** iOS = **dSYM bundle** (Xcode's Run Script build phase uploads it automatically via the Crashlytics tool); Android = **ProGuard/R8 mapping.txt** (Gradle plugin uploads if `mappingFileUploadEnabled true`) + optional **native symbols zip** for NDK (`nativeSymbolUploadEnabled true`); Flutter = **debug-info directory** from `--obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols`, upload via `firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload`. **Automate all three in CI** — Fastlane / GitHub Actions / Codemagic — and *fail the build* if upload fails. A single missed release = an entire release's crashes unreadable + hours of triage lost.

**Q4: How do you triage a sudden crash spike right after a release?**

**A:** **(1) Confirm scope:** filter by the new app version — is it spiking? What % of sessions on that version are crashing? **(2) Get the signature:** open the top-crashing issue by session count; read the stack trace + custom keys. **(3) Slice:** by device (Redmi Note 9?), OS (Android 10?), country, tenant, network state. Often a spike is one-cohort — Android 10 + specific OEM Skia driver, for instance. **(4) Correlate:** cross-reference with Analytics (which screens users were on) + Performance (was there a slow network trace preceding it?) + Remote Config variant (are only variant-B users crashing?). **(5) Mitigate before fix:** flip a Remote Config kill switch to the previous variant / disable the offending feature; hotfix release later. **(6) Root-cause fix + regression test.** **Sr-eng answer highlight:** *never* debug live from log lines alone — the shortest path is Remote Config rollback, then investigate calmly.

**Q5: How do you keep Crashlytics compliant with GDPR / DPDPA?**

**A:** **(1) Consent gate:** on first launch, ask; if user declines telemetry, call `setCrashlyticsCollectionEnabled(false)` — no reports upload. **(2) Delete identifier on sign-out** — `setUserIdentifier('')`. **(3) NEVER put PII in custom keys / logs** — no emails, phone numbers, auth tokens, or free-text user input. Store the pseudonymous UID only. **(4) Provide data-deletion path** — Crashlytics allows deleting per-installation data on request. **(5) Region considerations** — Firebase stores data in Google's global infrastructure; disclose in privacy policy. **(6) Disable in employee builds** — don't pollute prod signal with QA crashes. **A senior gets asked how to prove opt-out really works** — the answer is a debug build + Charles Proxy to confirm no requests leave the device after `setCollectionEnabled(false)`.

**Q6: What are ANRs and how does Crashlytics report them?**

**A:** **ANR = Application Not Responding** — Android detects the main thread frozen ≥ 5 seconds and shows the user the 'App is not responding' dialog. Crashlytics captures ANRs **automatically on Android** (no code); reports show under a separate **ANR** tab. Common causes: sync IO on main thread (SharedPreferences init, disk-heavy Room queries, plugin channel blocking calls). **Attribution:** stack trace at the moment ANR fired. **Fix approach:** move to background isolate / coroutine, add StrictMode in debug builds, wrap plugin channel calls in `unawaited`/`Isolate.run`. **iOS analog:** iOS terminates the app after ~20s of watchdog timeouts — reported as `0x8BADF00D` (`ate bad food`) crash. Google Play now penalizes ANR rate — treat as first-class quality metric alongside crash-free-users.

## Real-world usage

- **Every major mobile team** — Duolingo, Alibaba, NYT, Airbnb — tracks crash-free-users daily; velocity alerts drive on-call.
- **Store rating correlation** — 1% drop in stability often maps to 0.2-0.3 rating drop after 2 weeks.
- **CI gate** — releases blocked if pre-release Firebase Test Lab run crashes.
- **Auto-rollback pipelines** — Crashlytics velocity alert → Cloud Function → Remote Config flip = automated rollback without engineer intervention.
- **NOT the same as Sentry / Bugsnag** — Crashlytics is free + Firebase-integrated but has less flexible querying; Sentry adds session replay + custom search but is paid. Many teams run both.

## Advanced notes

- **BigQuery export** — enable in console; join with Analytics + Performance events for cohort-level stability analysis.
- **Attribute by Remote Config variant** — set variant as a custom key; per-variant crash-free-users compared directly.
- **Sessions vs users vs events** — the console offers all three denominators; users is the default SLO.
- **`recordError(printDetails: false)`** — suppress double-print in release logs.
- **`sendUnsentReports() / deleteUnsentReports()`** — control queued reports when respecting user consent.
- **`didCrashOnPreviousExecution` / `checkForUnsentReports`** — detect if last session crashed to show a 'sorry, we crashed' dialog with a bug report form.
- **On-device symbolication (iOS)** — new SDK versions symbolicate on-device to reduce upload payload.
- **ANR heuristics** — turn on strict mode in debug + macrobenchmark critical flows to catch frozen frames before prod.
- **Cross-platform stack unification** — Flutter reports include both Dart + platform frames when the crash traverses platform channels.
- **Grouping tweaks** — mark a signature as `Common Issue` if you want to suppress alerting until fixed.
- **A/B rollout gates** — combine with Firebase Test Distribution to test a new variant with 5% of users before wider rollout.
